title: HHS Poverty Guidelines API (federal poverty level for program eligibility, ASPE)
agency: HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE)
questions: federal poverty level for a family of four in 2026
138 percent of FPL for a single adult in Alaska (Medicaid expansion limit)
poverty guidelines for household sizes 1 to 8 since 2020
how much the poverty guideline for a family of three grew from 2000 to 2026
income at 400 percent of the poverty level for a family of four, with the guideline year the ACA premium tax credit uses

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (one per year, state group and household size) and save the JSON page under the name shown, then upload the files. Without the links: the current year's three tables (48 contiguous states and DC, Alaska, Hawaii) are on https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines, and every earlier year's tables with its Federal Register notice are on https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines/prior-hhs-poverty-guidelines-federal-register-references; copy the rows needed (year, state group, household size, guideline in dollars) and cite the Federal Register notice.

cache.why: A few small JSON answers per run; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: The poverty guidelines are a work of the U.S. government published in the Federal Register, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).

citation: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation, HHS Poverty Guidelines ({dataset}), Poverty Guidelines API, aspe.hhs.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which program's year convention? Guidelines are named for the year they are issued (January), and each program sets its own effective date (school meals from July 1); ACA premium tax credits for coverage year Y use the guidelines of year Y-1; SNAP uses USDA's fiscal-year tables (from October 1). Default: the guidelines of the year the user names, said as such.
Which schedule: the 48 contiguous states and DC, Alaska or Hawaii? Default: the 48 states and DC (us), unless the question names Alaska or Hawaii.

use_instead.question: Poverty rates, people in poverty, or the Census poverty thresholds (statistical poverty measure) by place or group
use_instead.why: Census publishes the official poverty thresholds and poverty estimates (ACS, CPS ASEC); the HHS guidelines are an administrative eligibility measure.

use_instead.question: SNAP participation, benefits or state eligibility options
use_instead.why: USDA FNS program data and the SNAP State Options Report; SNAP's income limits come from USDA's own fiscal-year tables.

use_instead.question: Medicaid and CHIP enrollment or spending
use_instead.why: data.medicaid.gov holds enrollment and expenditure data; this pack gives only the income guidelines programs apply.
